title: 📝 A seasons letter: read and check ⭐⭐

questions.prompt:
Yassine writes to his friend Hana: "Dear Hana, greetings from my aunt's farm near Siliana! Today is 14 October. The weather is windy and cool, and the sky is cloudy. In the morning I wear a warm sweater and boots. My cousin Wissem and I enjoy collecting apples and walking in the fields. Next week we will go back to school. See you soon! Yassine"

Which season comes after the season of this letter?

options.text: spring
winter
summer
autumn

questions.explanation: The letter is dated 14 October, a month of autumn, and the season that comes after autumn is winter, which opens in December. Spring and summer come later in the year, and autumn is the season of the letter itself.

questions.prompt: Hana reads in Yassine's letter: "The weather is windy and cool, and the sky is cloudy." She tells her mother: "It is sunny and hot at the farm." Hana is wrong. Which correction is right?

options.text: No, it's windy and cool there.
No, it's wind and cool there.
No, it's rainy and cool there.
No, it's windy and cooler there.

questions.explanation: The letter gives the weather of the farm: windy and cool. The correction must keep those two adjectives, and windy is the adjective built from the noun wind. The noun wind cannot be used as a description, rainy adds a weather the letter never mentions, and cooler compares the weather with something the letter does not name.

questions.prompt: Hana reads in Yassine's letter: "In the morning I wear a warm sweater and boots." She tells her mother: "Yassine wears shorts and a swimsuit in the morning." Hana is wrong. Which correction is right?

options.text: No, he wears a warm sweater and gloves.
No, he wears shorts and boots.
No, he wears a warm sweater and boots.
No, he wears a swimsuit and a sweater.

questions.explanation: The letter names two clothes for the morning: a warm sweater and boots, and the correction must give exactly those two. Gloves feel natural on a cool morning, but the letter never says that Yassine wears them, and the two other corrections keep one of the summer clothes that Hana got wrong.

questions.prompt: Hana reads in Yassine's letter: "My cousin Wissem and I enjoy collecting apples and walking in the fields." She tells her mother: "Yassine and Wissem enjoy swimming in the sea." Hana is wrong. Which correction is right?

options.text: No, they enjoy collect apples and walking in the fields.
No, they enjoy collecting apples and to walk in the fields.
No, they enjoy collecting apples and walkking in the fields.
No, they enjoy collecting apples and walking in the fields.

questions.explanation: The letter gives two activities, and after enjoy each activity takes the -ing form: collecting apples and walking in the fields. The bare verb collect and the form with to never follow enjoy, and walkking doubles a letter that comes after another consonant, where nothing is doubled.

questions.prompt: Hana reads in Yassine's letter: "Next week we will go back to school." She tells her mother: "Yassine goes back to school today." Hana is wrong. Which correction is right?

options.text: No, he will go back to school next week.
No, he will goes back to school next week.
No, he will to go back to school next week.
No, he wills go back to school next week.

questions.explanation: Next week is after today, so the sentence takes will, and after will the verb stays bare: he will go back. The word will never takes an -s, the verb after it never takes one either, and no to comes between the two.

questions.prompt: Hana writes back to Yassine and tells him about her own town: it is cold, there is snow and there is fog, so she wears gloves and boots. Complete her sentence: "Here it's ___ and ___ , so I wear gloves and boots."

options.text: snowwy ... foggy
snowy ... foggy
snowy ... fogy
snowwy ... fogy

questions.explanation: After It's the weather is described with adjectives: snow plus y gives snowy with no doubling, because snow ends in a w, and fog is consonant plus vowel plus consonant, so the g doubles in foggy. The spelling snowwy doubles a letter that is never doubled, and fogy forgets the doubling of fog.
